pr.title: drt: Add closed-loop adaptive search-and-repair policy
pr.body:
## Summary
Adds an opt-in closed-loop adaptive search-and-repair schedule (`detailed_route -adaptive_strategy`, implemented via `FlexDR::nextStepStrategy()` in `src/drt/src/dr/FlexDR.cpp`) discovered via AlphaEvolve alongside the baseline `strategy()` table. The policy was evolved on 5 ISPD benchmarks (marked with `*` in Table 1: `ispd18_test1`, `ispd18_test2`, `ispd18_test3`, `ispd18_test5`, `ispd19_test5`); although it generalizes well across the remaining 34 held-out ISPD and ORFS designs, there may be routing scenarios or PDK rules we were not aware of during evolution, so it is guarded behind `-adaptive_strategy` (off by default, leaving default `detailed_route` behavior completely unchanged for all existing users).

> **Note:** The opt-in `-adaptive_strategy` flag (`ParamStruct::adaptiveStrategy` / `RouterConfiguration::ADAPTIVE_STRATEGY`), explicit `FlexDRFlow::setStubbornFlowViolationThreshold()` configuration, C++ unit tests (`src/drt/test/AdaptiveStrategyTest.cpp`), and Tcl integration test (`src/drt/test/ispd18_sample_adaptive.tcl`) are included in this PR.

When `detailed_route -adaptive_strategy` is enabled, instead of stepping through the fixed 65-row baseline `strategy()` table by iteration index regardless of routing progress for all designs and PDKs, `nextStepStrategy()` selects `SearchRepairArgs` (`size`, `offset`, `mazeEndIter`, `drcCost`, `markerCost`, `fixedShapeCost`, `markerDecay`, `ripupMode`, `followGuide`) at each iteration `it >= 1` using the live DRV count, relative per-iteration DRV reduction rate, and consecutive stagnant-step count:
- **Unchanged below 700 initial DRVs across all PDKs (`history_drvs[0] < kAdaptiveMinInitialDrvs = 700`):** Small designs, `drt` unit tests (including `ispd18_sample`), and incremental repair passes that start with `< 700` DRVs after `it = 0` delegate directly to the baseline `strategy()` table across all PDKs (both bidirectional and unidirectional, including `asap7/gcd`, `nangate45/gcd`, and `sky130hd/gcd`) to keep outputs bit-exact.
- **Larger bidirectional designs (`it >= 1`, `history_drvs[0] >= 700`):** Replaces the early whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes (`it = 1, 2`) with targeted `RipUpMode::DRC` passes and dynamically escalates `ripupMode` (`DRC -> NEARDRC -> 3x3 ALL`), window `size` (`3..11`), `offset`, and `mazeEndIter` based on DRV reduction rate and stall count (including a post-`NEARDRC` DRV-spike settle pass in high-DRV regimes, steeper DRC costs for moderate post-`it=1` designs with `500 <= history_drvs[1] < 600`, and fallback to baseline `strategy[30..64]` in deep tails).
- **Larger unidirectional PDK designs (`it >= 1`, `history_drvs[0] >= 700`, e.g., `asap7` `aes`, `ibex`, `jpeg`, `ethmac`):** Runs the first shifted `RipUpMode::ALL` pass (`strategy[1]`, `offset = -2`) to straighten `it = 0` tile-boundary seams, skips the redundant second `RipUpMode::ALL` pass (`strategy[2]`, `offset = -5`), and lowers the `FlexDRFlow` stubborn-flow violation threshold (`setStubbornFlowViolationThreshold(kAdaptiveUnidirStubbornThreshold = 15)`) so `FlexDRFlow` stays in `optimizationFlow` until `num_markers <= 15`.

## Type of Change
- New feature

## Impact
Across 39 benchmarks (`20` ISPD-18/19 contest designs and `19` end-to-end ORFS designs across `nangate45`, `sky130hd`, and `asap7`), enabling `-adaptive_strategy` reduces search-and-repair (`S&R`) runtime by 2.50x overall (2.14x geomean, 39/39 designs faster or bit-exact) with 0 DRC regressions:

| Benchmark Suite | Designs | DRVs (`Base` / `PR`) | Base S&R (s) | PR S&R (s) | S&R Speedup (Agg / Geo) | WL $\Delta$ | Via $\Delta$ |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1. ISPD-18 & ISPD-19** | 20 | `19/20` at `0` (`test10`: `14` $\rightarrow$ `13`) | 17,649.0 | 6,334.0 | 2.79x / 2.79x | +0.41% | +1.94% |
| **2. ORFS Small/Medium** (`asap7`, `nangate45`, `sky130hd`) | 12 | `12/12` at `0` | 2,270.0 | 1,515.0 | 1.50x / 1.41x | +0.51% | +0.83% |
| **3. ORFS Large SoCs** (`asap7`, `nangate45`) | 7 | `7/7` at `0` | 2,378.0 | 1,086.0 | 2.19x / 2.07x | +0.40% | +1.48% |
| **Combined Total** | 39 | `38/38` solvable at `0` | 22,297.0 | 8,935.0 | 2.50x / 2.14x | +0.44% | +1.51% |

**Quality of Results (DRVs, Wirelength, Via Count, and Timing):**
- **DRVs:** Total DRV count matches or is lower than baseline across all 39 designs (`0` DRVs on all 38 solvable designs, and `13` vs. `14` DRVs on `ispd19_test10`).
- **Wirelength (worst case `+1.11%` on `sky130hd/jpeg`) and Via Count (worst case `+2.92%` on `ispd19_test10` and `+1.87%` among ORFS designs on `nangate45/bp_fe`):** During `it = 0` (`size = 7, offset = 0, RipUpMode::ALL`), `FlexDR` routes `7x7` GCell boxes independently and connects nets at track-assignment boundary pins (`gcell2BoundaryPin_`), which leaves small jogs and boundary vias where adjacent tiles pick different tracks even when DRC-clean. The baseline `strategy()` straightens these DRC-clean boundary seams by running two whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes at `it = 1` (`offset = -2`) and `it = 2` (`offset = -5`). Skipping those whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes in favor of targeted `RipUpMode::DRC` passes yields the `2.50x` S&R speedup while leaving those `~1–2%` boundary vias in place; running an additional shifted `RipUpMode::ALL` pass at `it = 1` (as done for unidirectional layers) reduces the via and wirelength delta toward baseline at the cost of one extra whole-chip pass.
- **Timing:** Timing was not part of the optimization objective during evolution, as only ISPD-18 and ISPD-19 benchmarks (which contain physical LEF/DEF/guide files without timing libraries or constraints) were used in the evolution.

data.summary: This PR introduces an opt-in closed-loop adaptive search-and-repair strategy for the `detailed_route` command, which dynamically adjusts routing parameters based on real-time DRV counts and progress to improve search-and-repair runtime.

evidence.claim: The new adaptive strategy is an opt-in feature that does not change default behavior.
evidence.quote: guarded behind `-adaptive_strategy` (off by default, leaving default `detailed_route` behavior completely unchanged for all existing users).

evidence.claim: The implementation includes both C++ and Tcl-based testing.
evidence.quote: C++ unit tests (`src/drt/test/AdaptiveStrategyTest.cpp`), and Tcl integration test (`src/drt/test/ispd18_sample_adaptive.tcl`) are included in this PR.

## Summary
Adds an opt-in closed-loop adaptive search-and-repair schedule (`detailed_route -adaptive_strategy`, implemented via `FlexDR::nextStepStrategy()` in `src/drt/src/dr/FlexDR.cpp`) discovered via AlphaEvolve alongside the baseline `strategy()` table. The policy was evolved on 5 ISPD benchmarks (marked with `*` in Table 1: `ispd18_test1`, `ispd18_test2`, `ispd18_test3`, `ispd18_test5`, `ispd19_test5`); although it generalizes well across the remaining 34 held-out ISPD and ORFS designs, there may be routing scenarios or PDK rules we were not aware of during evolution, so it is guarded behind `-adaptive_strategy` (off by default, leaving default `detailed_route` behavior completely unchanged for all existing users).

> **Note:** The opt-in `-adaptive_strategy` flag (`ParamStruct::adaptiveStrategy` / `RouterConfiguration::ADAPTIVE_STRATEGY`), explicit `FlexDRFlow::setStubbornFlowViolationThreshold()` configuration, C++ unit tests (`src/drt/test/AdaptiveStrategyTest.cpp`), and Tcl integration test (`src/drt/test/ispd18_sample_adaptive.tcl`) are included in this PR.

When `detailed_route -adaptive_strategy` is enabled, instead of stepping through the fixed 65-row baseline `strategy()` table by iteration index regardless of routing progress for all designs and PDKs, `nextStepStrategy()` selects `SearchRepairArgs` (`size`, `offset`, `mazeEndIter`, `drcCost`, `markerCost`, `fixedShapeCost`, `markerDecay`, `ripupMode`, `followGuide`) at each iteration `it >= 1` using the live DRV count, relative per-iteration DRV reduction rate, and consecutive stagnant-step count:
- **Unchanged below 700 initial DRVs across all PDKs (`history_drvs[0] < kAdaptiveMinInitialDrvs = 700`):** Small designs, `drt` unit tests (including `ispd18_sample`), and incremental repair passes that start with `< 700` DRVs after `it = 0` delegate directly to the baseline `strategy()` table across all PDKs (both bidirectional and unidirectional, including `asap7/gcd`, `nangate45/gcd`, and `sky130hd/gcd`) to keep outputs bit-exact.
- **Larger bidirectional designs (`it >= 1`, `history_drvs[0] >= 700`):** Replaces the early whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes (`it = 1, 2`) with targeted `RipUpMode::DRC` passes and dynamically escalates `ripupMode` (`DRC -> NEARDRC -> 3x3 ALL`), window `size` (`3..11`), `offset`, and `mazeEndIter` based on DRV reduction rate and stall count (including a post-`NEARDRC` DRV-spike settle pass in high-DRV regimes, steeper DRC costs for moderate post-`it=1` designs with `500 <= history_drvs[1] < 600`, and fallback to baseline `strategy[30..64]` in deep tails).
- **Larger unidirectional PDK designs (`it >= 1`, `history_drvs[0] >= 700`, e.g., `asap7` `aes`, `ibex`, `jpeg`, `ethmac`):** Runs the first shifted `RipUpMode::ALL` pass (`strategy[1]`, `offset = -2`) to straighten `it = 0` tile-boundary seams, skips the redundant second `RipUpMode::ALL` pass (`strategy[2]`, `offset = -5`), and lowers the `FlexDRFlow` stubborn-flow violation threshold (`setStubbornFlowViolationThreshold(kAdaptiveUnidirStubbornThreshold = 15)`) so `FlexDRFlow` stays in `optimizationFlow` until `num_markers <= 15`.

## Type of Change
- New feature

## Impact
Across 39 benchmarks (`20` ISPD-18/19 contest designs and `19` end-to-end ORFS designs across `nangate45`, `sky130hd`, and `asap7`), enabling `-adaptive_strategy` reduces search-and-repair (`S&R`) runtime by 2.50x overall (2.14x geomean, 39/39 designs faster or bit-exact) with 0 DRC regressions:

| Benchmark Suite | Designs | DRVs (`Base` / `PR`) | Base S&R (s) | PR S&R (s) | S&R Speedup (Agg / Geo) | WL $\Delta$ | Via $\Delta$ |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1. ISPD-18 & ISPD-19** | 20 | `19/20` at `0` (`test10`: `14` $\rightarrow$ `13`) | 17,649.0 | 6,334.0 | 2.79x / 2.79x | +0.41% | +1.94% |
| **2. ORFS Small/Medium** (`asap7`, `nangate45`, `sky130hd`) | 12 | `12/12` at `0` | 2,270.0 | 1,515.0 | 1.50x / 1.41x | +0.51% | +0.83% |
| **3. ORFS Large SoCs** (`asap7`, `nangate45`) | 7 | `7/7` at `0` | 2,378.0 | 1,086.0 | 2.19x / 2.07x | +0.40% | +1.48% |
| **Combined Total** | 39 | `38/38` solvable at `0` | 22,297.0 | 8,935.0 | 2.50x / 2.14x | +0.44% | +1.51% |

**Quality of Results (DRVs, Wirelength, Via Count, and Timing):**
- **DRVs:** Total DRV count matches or is lower than baseline across all 39 designs (`0` DRVs on all 38 solvable designs, and `13` vs. `14` DRVs on `ispd19_test10`).
- **Wirelength (worst case `+1.11%` on `sky130hd/jpeg`) and Via Count (worst case `+2.92%` on `ispd19_test10` and `+1.87%` among ORFS designs on `nangate45/bp_fe`):** During `it = 0` (`size = 7, offset = 0, RipUpMode::ALL`), `FlexDR` routes `7x7` GCell boxes independently and connects nets at track-assignment boundary pins (`gcell2BoundaryPin_`), which leaves small jogs and boundary vias where adjacent tiles pick different tracks even when DRC-clean. The baseline `strategy()` straightens these DRC-clean boundary seams by running two whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes at `it = 1` (`offset = -2`) and `it = 2` (`offset = -5`). Skipping those whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes in favor of targeted `RipUpMode::DRC` passes yields the `2.50x` S&R speedup while leaving those `~1–2%` boundary vias in place; running an additional shifted `RipUpMode::ALL` pass at `it = 1` (as done for unidirectional layers) reduces the via and wirelength delta toward baseline at the cost of one extra whole-chip pass.
- **Timing:** Timing was not part of the optimization objective during evolution, as only ISPD-18 and ISPD-19 benchmarks (which contain physical LEF/DEF/guide files without timing libraries or constraints) were used in the evolution.

# Contributing to OpenROAD

Thank you for contributing to OpenROAD. For setup, coding standards,
and workflow details, see the existing guides:

- [Getting Involved](docs/contrib/GettingInvolved.md) -- how to contribute, licensing, DCO
- [Developer Guide](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md) -- architecture, tool structure, testing
- [Coding Practices](docs/contrib/CodingPractices.md) -- C++ style and idioms
- [Logger Guide](docs/contrib/Logger.md) -- logging API for C++ and Tcl

## Review Priorities

Reviews are prioritized in this order:

### 1. Correctness

The most important concern. Code must produce correct results.

- Flag any code that could silently produce wrong output. An explicit
  error is always preferable to silently incorrect behavior.
- Watch for classic bugs: iterator invalidation, use-after-free,
  off-by-one, integer overflow in area calculations (use `int64_t`
  for area), deleting from a container while iterating over it.
- Code after `error()` or `throw` is unreachable -- remove it.
- If a test is being disabled or suppressed, ask whether it is hiding
  a real bug.

### 2. Quality of Results (QoR) Impact

Any change that could affect placement, routing, timing, or other
physical design metrics must be validated.

- Ask: "Does this have a QoR impact?" Changes affecting QoR require
  validation on real designs, not just unit tests. Maintainers will
  trigger the necessary CI runs for this.
- Be skeptical of QoR improvements claimed from a single design.
  Improvements should be validated across multiple designs and
  technologies.

### 3. Testing

Every code change should have accompanying tests. See the
[Developer Guide](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md#test) for test
conventions.

### 4. Architecture and Dependencies

OpenROAD is a single-process, single-database tool. See the
[Developer Guide](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md#tool-philosophy) for
architectural guidelines and the
[tool checklist](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md#tool-checklist).

### 5. C++ Style and Logging

We follow the [Google C++ style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html).
See [Coding Practices](docs/contrib/CodingPractices.md) for
project-specific idioms and the
[Logger Guide](docs/contrib/Logger.md) for the logging API.

### 6. Process

- Every commit must include a DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`).
- CI must be green before review. Reviewers may not look at
  failing PRs.
- Keep PRs focused on one bug or feature. Style fixes go in separate
  commits.
- Reference an open issue for non-trivial changes.
- Mac builds are best-effort and not merge-blocking.

## For AI/LLM Code Reviewers

When reviewing OpenROAD pull requests, follow the priority order above.
Focus review comments on correctness and QoR impact rather than style
nitpicks -- `clang-tidy` and `clang-format` handle style automatically.

Specific guidance:

- **Be concise.** One-word or one-sentence comments are preferred when
  the issue is clear (e.g., "const", "unreachable after throw").
- **Ask probing questions** rather than prescribing fixes for
  non-obvious issues (e.g., "Have you tested this on a real design?"
  or "Could this hide a bug?").
- **Flag QoR-affecting changes** that lack validation on real designs.
- **Don't generate summaries** of the PR unless asked. The config
  disables automatic summaries.
- **Do flag** unreachable code after `error()`/`throw`, missing
  `const`, null pointer issues, iterator invalidation, and missing
  tests.
- **Don't flag** style issues already covered by `clang-format` or
  `clang-tidy`.
- **Check database schema changes** -- any change to the ODB schema
  requires a revision bump to prevent old versions from misinterpreting
  new data.
- **Watch for memory concerns** -- `dbITerm` and similar objects are
  numerous. Adding fields to heavily-instantiated classes has real
  memory cost.

## License

Contributions should use the BSD-3-Clause license. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

source_corpus.title: drt: Add closed-loop adaptive search-and-repair policy
source_corpus.body:
## Summary
Adds an opt-in closed-loop adaptive search-and-repair schedule (`detailed_route -adaptive_strategy`, implemented via `FlexDR::nextStepStrategy()` in `src/drt/src/dr/FlexDR.cpp`) discovered via AlphaEvolve alongside the baseline `strategy()` table. The policy was evolved on 5 ISPD benchmarks (marked with `*` in Table 1: `ispd18_test1`, `ispd18_test2`, `ispd18_test3`, `ispd18_test5`, `ispd19_test5`); although it generalizes well across the remaining 34 held-out ISPD and ORFS designs, there may be routing scenarios or PDK rules we were not aware of during evolution, so it is guarded behind `-adaptive_strategy` (off by default, leaving default `detailed_route` behavior completely unchanged for all existing users).

> **Note:** The opt-in `-adaptive_strategy` flag (`ParamStruct::adaptiveStrategy` / `RouterConfiguration::ADAPTIVE_STRATEGY`), explicit `FlexDRFlow::setStubbornFlowViolationThreshold()` configuration, C++ unit tests (`src/drt/test/AdaptiveStrategyTest.cpp`), and Tcl integration test (`src/drt/test/ispd18_sample_adaptive.tcl`) are included in this PR.

When `detailed_route -adaptive_strategy` is enabled, instead of stepping through the fixed 65-row baseline `strategy()` table by iteration index regardless of routing progress for all designs and PDKs, `nextStepStrategy()` selects `SearchRepairArgs` (`size`, `offset`, `mazeEndIter`, `drcCost`, `markerCost`, `fixedShapeCost`, `markerDecay`, `ripupMode`, `followGuide`) at each iteration `it >= 1` using the live DRV count, relative per-iteration DRV reduction rate, and consecutive stagnant-step count:
- **Unchanged below 700 initial DRVs across all PDKs (`history_drvs[0] < kAdaptiveMinInitialDrvs = 700`):** Small designs, `drt` unit tests (including `ispd18_sample`), and incremental repair passes that start with `< 700` DRVs after `it = 0` delegate directly to the baseline `strategy()` table across all PDKs (both bidirectional and unidirectional, including `asap7/gcd`, `nangate45/gcd`, and `sky130hd/gcd`) to keep outputs bit-exact.
- **Larger bidirectional designs (`it >= 1`, `history_drvs[0] >= 700`):** Replaces the early whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes (`it = 1, 2`) with targeted `RipUpMode::DRC` passes and dynamically escalates `ripupMode` (`DRC -> NEARDRC -> 3x3 ALL`), window `size` (`3..11`), `offset`, and `mazeEndIter` based on DRV reduction rate and stall count (including a post-`NEARDRC` DRV-spike settle pass in high-DRV regimes, steeper DRC costs for moderate post-`it=1` designs with `500 <= history_drvs[1] < 600`, and fallback to baseline `strategy[30..64]` in deep tails).
- **Larger unidirectional PDK designs (`it >= 1`, `history_drvs[0] >= 700`, e.g., `asap7` `aes`, `ibex`, `jpeg`, `ethmac`):** Runs the first shifted `RipUpMode::ALL` pass (`strategy[1]`, `offset = -2`) to straighten `it = 0` tile-boundary seams, skips the redundant second `RipUpMode::ALL` pass (`strategy[2]`, `offset = -5`), and lowers the `FlexDRFlow` stubborn-flow violation threshold (`setStubbornFlowViolationThreshold(kAdaptiveUnidirStubbornThreshold = 15)`) so `FlexDRFlow` stays in `optimizationFlow` until `num_markers <= 15`.

## Type of Change
- New feature

## Impact
Across 39 benchmarks (`20` ISPD-18/19 contest designs and `19` end-to-end ORFS designs across `nangate45`, `sky130hd`, and `asap7`), enabling `-adaptive_strategy` reduces search-and-repair (`S&R`) runtime by 2.50x overall (2.14x geomean, 39/39 designs faster or bit-exact) with 0 DRC regressions:

| Benchmark Suite | Designs | DRVs (`Base` / `PR`) | Base S&R (s) | PR S&R (s) | S&R Speedup (Agg / Geo) | WL $\Delta$ | Via $\Delta$ |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1. ISPD-18 & ISPD-19** | 20 | `19/20` at `0` (`test10`: `14` $\rightarrow$ `13`) | 17,649.0 | 6,334.0 | 2.79x / 2.79x | +0.41% | +1.94% |
| **2. ORFS Small/Medium** (`asap7`, `nangate45`, `sky130hd`) | 12 | `12/12` at `0` | 2,270.0 | 1,515.0 | 1.50x / 1.41x | +0.51% | +0.83% |
| **3. ORFS Large SoCs** (`asap7`, `nangate45`) | 7 | `7/7` at `0` | 2,378.0 | 1,086.0 | 2.19x / 2.07x | +0.40% | +1.48% |
| **Combined Total** | 39 | `38/38` solvable at `0` | 22,297.0 | 8,935.0 | 2.50x / 2.14x | +0.44% | +1.51% |

**Quality of Results (DRVs, Wirelength, Via Count, and Timing):**
- **DRVs:** Total DRV count matches or is lower than baseline across all 39 designs (`0` DRVs on all 38 solvable designs, and `13` vs. `14` DRVs on `ispd19_test10`).
- **Wirelength (worst case `+1.11%` on `sky130hd/jpeg`) and Via Count (worst case `+2.92%` on `ispd19_test10` and `+1.87%` among ORFS designs on `nangate45/bp_fe`):** During `it = 0` (`size = 7, offset = 0, RipUpMode::ALL`), `FlexDR` routes `7x7` GCell boxes independently and connects nets at track-assignment boundary pins (`gcell2BoundaryPin_`), which leaves small jogs and boundary vias where adjacent tiles pick different tracks even when DRC-clean. The baseline `strategy()` straightens these DRC-clean boundary seams by running two whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes at `it = 1` (`offset = -2`) and `it = 2` (`offset = -5`). Skipping those whole-chip `RipUpMode::ALL` passes in favor of targeted `RipUpMode::DRC` passes yields the `2.50x` S&R speedup while leaving those `~1–2%` boundary vias in place; running an additional shifted `RipUpMode::ALL` pass at `it = 1` (as done for unidirectional layers) reduces the via and wirelength delta toward baseline at the cost of one extra whole-chip pass.
- **Timing:** Timing was not part of the optimization objective during evolution, as only ISPD-18 and ISPD-19 benchmarks (which contain physical LEF/DEF/guide files without timing libraries or constraints) were used in the evolution.

# Contributing to OpenROAD

Thank you for contributing to OpenROAD. For setup, coding standards,
and workflow details, see the existing guides:

- [Getting Involved](docs/contrib/GettingInvolved.md) -- how to contribute, licensing, DCO
- [Developer Guide](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md) -- architecture, tool structure, testing
- [Coding Practices](docs/contrib/CodingPractices.md) -- C++ style and idioms
- [Logger Guide](docs/contrib/Logger.md) -- logging API for C++ and Tcl

## Review Priorities

Reviews are prioritized in this order:

### 1. Correctness

The most important concern. Code must produce correct results.

- Flag any code that could silently produce wrong output. An explicit
  error is always preferable to silently incorrect behavior.
- Watch for classic bugs: iterator invalidation, use-after-free,
  off-by-one, integer overflow in area calculations (use `int64_t`
  for area), deleting from a container while iterating over it.
- Code after `error()` or `throw` is unreachable -- remove it.
- If a test is being disabled or suppressed, ask whether it is hiding
  a real bug.

### 2. Quality of Results (QoR) Impact

Any change that could affect placement, routing, timing, or other
physical design metrics must be validated.

- Ask: "Does this have a QoR impact?" Changes affecting QoR require
  validation on real designs, not just unit tests. Maintainers will
  trigger the necessary CI runs for this.
- Be skeptical of QoR improvements claimed from a single design.
  Improvements should be validated across multiple designs and
  technologies.

### 3. Testing

Every code change should have accompanying tests. See the
[Developer Guide](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md#test) for test
conventions.

### 4. Architecture and Dependencies

OpenROAD is a single-process, single-database tool. See the
[Developer Guide](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md#tool-philosophy) for
architectural guidelines and the
[tool checklist](docs/contrib/DeveloperGuide.md#tool-checklist).

### 5. C++ Style and Logging

We follow the [Google C++ style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html).
See [Coding Practices](docs/contrib/CodingPractices.md) for
project-specific idioms and the
[Logger Guide](docs/contrib/Logger.md) for the logging API.

### 6. Process

- Every commit must include a DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`).
- CI must be green before review. Reviewers may not look at
  failing PRs.
- Keep PRs focused on one bug or feature. Style fixes go in separate
  commits.
- Reference an open issue for non-trivial changes.
- Mac builds are best-effort and not merge-blocking.

## For AI/LLM Code Reviewers

When reviewing OpenROAD pull requests, follow the priority order above.
Focus review comments on correctness and QoR impact rather than style
nitpicks -- `clang-tidy` and `clang-format` handle style automatically.

Specific guidance:

- **Be concise.** One-word or one-sentence comments are preferred when
  the issue is clear (e.g., "const", "unreachable after throw").
- **Ask probing questions** rather than prescribing fixes for
  non-obvious issues (e.g., "Have you tested this on a real design?"
  or "Could this hide a bug?").
- **Flag QoR-affecting changes** that lack validation on real designs.
- **Don't generate summaries** of the PR unless asked. The config
  disables automatic summaries.
- **Do flag** unreachable code after `error()`/`throw`, missing
  `const`, null pointer issues, iterator invalidation, and missing
  tests.
- **Don't flag** style issues already covered by `clang-format` or
  `clang-tidy`.
- **Check database schema changes** -- any change to the ODB schema
  requires a revision bump to prevent old versions from misinterpreting
  new data.
- **Watch for memory concerns** -- `dbITerm` and similar objects are
  numerous. Adding fields to heavily-instantiated classes has real
  memory cost.

## License

Contributions should use the BSD-3-Clause license. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
